title: Investigate the Great Fire of London
audience: Curious secondary learners and adults, including people uninterested in history
level: Introductory historical inquiry, no prior Great Fire study assumed
outcomes: Separate observation from inference with explicit uncertainty
Evaluate provenance, purpose and limits of a historical source
Corroborate independent accounts using maps and chronology
Build a defensible multi-causal explanation and acknowledge alternatives
prerequisites: Read a short adapted source; read a labelled schematic map and chronological sequence
scope: Four source-based investigations of the September 1666 fire, its spread, accounts and explanations
excluded: A single mechanically correct interpretation of contested evidence
sources: London Museum Great Fire and myths pages
Primary Pepys diary September 1666, provenance to verify before drafting
Digital Inquiry Group historical inquiry guidance
playConcept: A case file with maps and time-stamped evidence: inspect witnesses in different orders, distinguish seen from inferred, corroborate and assemble a defensible account with limits.
decisions: Authored source adaptations will be explicitly labelled
Open causal claims use rubric reflection/human review, never runtime AI marking
assumptions: Timeline and map knowledge can be introduced through interactions
